findings.evidence: Auslander–Reiten–Smalø VII.1 (from recollection, not checked against the text): the valuation (a,b) of an arrow is the pair of dimensions of Irr(X,Y) over the two residue division rings; neither alone counts arrows.
findings.fix: In all three places, say the valued arrow X → Y exists iff Irr(X,Y) ≠ 0 and its valuation is the pair of the two ranks; drop 'the target-side one'/'the target's'.
findings.issue: Module docstring says the textbook convention counts the arrows X → Y of a valued AR quiver by one rank, 'the target-side one'. A valued quiver has a single arrow X → Y when Irr(X,Y) ≠ 0, carrying the pair of ranks over both residue division rings as its valuation; the same claim recurs in the docstring of rank_irreducibleMorphismSpace_pos_iff (line 360-366) and in TauCeti/RingTheory/LocalRing/Residue.lean:25 ('the rank over one of those division rings, the target's').

findings.evidence: ASS Vol. 1 assumes k algebraically closed throughout (from recollection); its AR quiver has dim_k Irr(M,N) arrows M → N.
findings.fix: Attribute the residue-division-ring/valued-quiver convention to Auslander–Reiten–Smalø VII.1, and cite ASS only for the k-dimension count over an algebraically closed field (or drop the parenthetical).
findings.issue: The reference to Assem–Simson–Skowroński Vol. 1 claims the AR-quiver arrows are counted there by the dimensions of rad/rad² over the residue division rings. ASS Vol. 1 works over an algebraically closed field and uses dim_k Irr(M,N); residue division rings and valued quivers are not its convention.

summary: The new files and public declarations are documented, but several docstrings misdescribe the valued Auslander-Reiten quiver as counting arrows by the target-side rank alone, and one reference misattributes the residue-division-ring convention to Assem–Simson–Skowroński.
